claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute, a cloud-provider deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute, a cloud-provider deletion-protection setting separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
Cloud-provider deletion-protection attributes such as `deletionProtection` are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (`protect` not set) and still refuse to be deleted because of a provider-side deletion-protection attribute, or vice versa.

The docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section titled 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi `protect` and provider-side deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, which the provider or the cloud API enforces independently.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion-protection setting) in the Pulumi GCP provider.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion-protection setting) in the Pulumi AWS provider.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attributes are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page on destroy failures has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' (at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/#deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself) explaining how to tell `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.

Three distinct layers can hold deletion protection that causes a `pulumi destroy` failure (Pulumi's `protect` option, a provider-enforced flag, and a cloud-API-enforced protection), and the error message usually indicates which one was hit.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails on a protected resource, the error names a URN and mentions `protect`.
A page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ explaining how to remove the `protect` resource option.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/run-program/ titled 'Running your program on refresh and destroy'.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, and the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks cause the cloud API itself to reject the delete call, independent of Pulumi.
Cloud-API-enforced deletion protection errors come back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says.

Setting a deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program is not enough on its own to allow `pulumi destroy` to succeed; the remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced protection is the same.
To remove deletion protection: set the attribute to `false` in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches both the live resource and Pulumi's state, then run `pulumi destroy`.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`; a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to `false`.
Azure management locks are represented in Pulumi by `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`.
Azure Resource Manager enforces management locks; a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
